focus: What a vision model can and cannot read from a UI screenshot, and which reads Flow Mode must re-check or refuse
answeredQuestions: What can a vision-capable model reliably read from a UI screenshot, and which reads must Flow Mode re-check or refuse?

label: The default local vision checkpoint cannot transcribe text and the OCR-capable one is labelled approximate, so a node label retyped from a screenshot is an unverified transcription that Flow Mode never marks

The vision scene read classifies type, layout, elements and state but returns no coordinates, so the click target Flow Mode reads off an image is a description unless a point or detect call is made, and the packet names neither
Small text fails at full-image scale and only a second read on an upscaled crop makes it readable, so a label read once from a dense screenshot must be re-read on a crop before it is written
A pixel diff between two screenshots returns a changed percentage and up to twelve changed-region boxes, which settles new screen versus new state without a caption, and Flow Mode has no such test

Figma's own screenshot-reading workflow carries a per-item uncertainty vocabulary (unknown trigger, inferred, uncertain, visible false, confidence medium or low) that suppresses a guessed marker by default, while Flow Mode has only a prose never-invent rule and no per-item marker
The before/after pair rather than the screenshot is the unit that carries a trigger, so the intake record should be from, to, trigger and confidence instead of a flat ordered file list

direction: Treat sk_vision_ocr as an exact transcription channel for node labels
reason: The skill states the OCR checkpoint is a preview that can repeat tokens and must be verified against ground truth
